legend: Tingyun gives you an array a$$$a$$$ of size n$$$n$$$.
Given an integer x$$$x$$$, define functions f0(x),f1(x),…,fn(x)$$$f_0(x),f_1(x),\ldots,f_n(x)$$$ as follows:
fk(x)=fk−1(x) mod ak$$$f_k(x)=f_{k-1}(x) \text{ mod } a_k$$$ for any integer k>0$$$k \gt 0$$$.
In other words, fn(x)=(…((x mod a1) mod a2)… mod an)$$$f_n(x) = (\ldots((x \text{ mod } a_1)\text{ mod } a_2)\ldots \text{ mod } a_n)$$$.

Note for positive integers a$$$a$$$ and b$$$b$$$, a mod b$$$a \text{ mod } b$$$ is the unique integer 0≤c<b$$$0\leq c  \lt  b$$$ such that a−c$$$a-c$$$ is divisible by b$$$b$$$. For example, 5 mod 3=2$$$5 \text{ mod } 3 = 2$$$.
Tingyun then gives you q$$$q$$$ values of x$$$x$$$. For each x$$$x$$$, please output the value of fn(x)$$$f_n(x)$$$.
input: The first line contains an integer t$$$t$$$ – the number of test cases (1≤t≤104$$$1 \leq t \leq 10^4$$$).
The first line of each test case contains two integers n$$$n$$$ and q$$$q$$$ (1≤n,q≤105$$$1 \leq n,q \leq 10^5$$$).
The second line of each test case contains n$$$n$$$ integers a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n$$$ (1≤ai≤109$$$1 \leq a_i \leq 10^9$$$).
The next q$$$q$$$ lines each contain an integer x$$$x$$$ (1≤x≤109$$$1 \leq x \leq 10^9$$$).
It is guaranteed that neither the sum of n$$$n$$$ nor the sum of q$$$q$$$ exceeds 105$$$10^5$$$ over all test cases.
Partial credits will be given to programs who pass tests with smaller constraints outlined below.
output: Output the answer for each x$$$x$$$ on a new line.
